items.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Template System
items.summary: This zero-day vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution by injecting malicious PHP code into Magento's template system, often triggered by a failed payment email. It has a CVSS score of 10.0 and was actively exploited in the wild.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This Adobe Security Bulletin addresses the critical CVE-2026-75650 vulnerability, which could lead to arbitrary code execution and was being exploited in the wild. Adobe released an emergency hotfix (VULN-39341) for affected versions.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This regularly scheduled security update resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities, including issues that could lead to security feature bypass and privilege escalation. Adobe was not aware of active exploits for the issues addressed in this bulletin at the time of publication.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization leading to Privilege Escalation
items.summary: An incorrect authorization vulnerability in Adobe Commerce and Magento allows an attacker to gain elevated access to sensitive resources without user interaction. This flaw has a CVSS score of 9.1 and has been added to the CISA KEV catalog due to evidence of active exploitation.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This security update addresses critical and important vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-71362, which could result in arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation. Adobe released isolated patch files to facilitate prompt remediation.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This bulletin resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities that could lead to arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, and security feature bypass. Adobe was not aware of any exploits in the wild for these issues at the time of release.

items.title: Improper Input Validation in Commerce REST API
items.summary: This vulnerability, publicly known as SessionReaper, allows an unauthenticated attacker to hijack customer sessions through the REST API and potentially achieve remote code execution. Although originally disclosed in 2025, Sansec reported ongoing active exploitation and that many stores remained vulnerable in September 2026.
